diagnosis.summary: The order-service Lambda function is executing far more slowly than normal, with mean handler duration rising from 2 ms to 352 ms. End-to-end latency has risen in parallel, with p95 now at 375 ms against a baseline of 24 ms. Request rate and 5xx error rate are both unchanged.
diagnosis.root_cause: Severe slowdown inside the order-service Lambda handler is the most likely root cause, with execution time inflated 176x while traffic and error rates remain stable.
evidence: Mean Lambda handler duration in order-service rose from 2 ms to 352 ms, a 176x increase.
Median end-to-end latency rose from 17 ms to 360 ms, a 21x increase.
p95 end-to-end latency rose from 24 ms to 375 ms, a 15.6x increase against baseline.
Request rate is flat at 2.9 rps, identical to the baseline of 2.9 rps.
5xx error rate remains at 0.0, unchanged from baseline.
recommended_actions: Review order-service Lambda CloudWatch logs for the incident window starting 2026-10-30T16:03:00Z for slow operations, timeouts, or unexpected execution paths inside the handler.
Check DynamoDB latency metrics for the order-service table to determine whether database call time is contributing to the elevated handler duration.
Inspect dependency latency metrics for order-service calls to payment-service to assess whether the payment integration is adding to handler execution time.
Review Lambda concurrency and memory utilisation for order-service to identify resource contention that may be slowing execution.
If a recent deployment or configuration change to order-service coincided with 16:03 UTC, consider rolling it back while the investigation continues.
